body.content: Speculative synthesis: the nocturnal UHI may be an interactive product of (1) sky-view-factor geometry trapping longwave radiation and (2) thermal-mass storage release. The cross-city modulator could be the PRODUCT of these two factors rather than either alone. A city with deep canyons but low thermal mass (e.g., lightweight informal construction) might trap radiation but have little stored heat to emit. A city with massive buildings but low density (e.g., a campus-style city) might store heat but radiate it freely to the sky. The largest UHI would occur where BOTH are high. This is a multiplicative hypothesis, not an additive one.
body.possible_next_move: Design a simulation that factorially crosses sky-view factor and thermal mass to test for interaction effects on nocturnal UHI magnitude.
body.unfinished: Need to check whether empirical UHI studies report interaction effects or only main effects of geometry and thermal mass.
body.why_keep_this: This multiplicative hypothesis is criticizable and could be overturned by cities that have large UHI with only one factor present.
